scholarships.title: DAAD Study Scholarships - Postgraduate Studies in the Field of the Performing Arts

existing.description: DAAD study scholarship for graduates in the performing arts to continue their education in Germany with a postgraduate or continuing course of study. Funding covers a Master's/postgraduate degree course or a one-year complementary course without degree at a state or state-recognised German university. The programme funds projects in the artistic field of the performing arts: Drama, Theatre Directing/Theatre Dramaturgy, Musicals, Performance Studies, Dance and Choreography. The scholarship pays a monthly stipend of EUR 992 plus a travel allowance, a one-off study allowance and insurance payments; it does not pay tuition fees.
eligibility: First university degree in the field of the arts, in the performing arts
University degree normally not older than 6 years at the application deadline
Not resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the application deadline
Nationality must be selectable in the DAAD portal together with the applicant's status
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must hold a first university degree in the field of the Performing Arts by the time they commence the scholarship-supported study programme. The degree should normally not be more than 6 years old at the application deadline, study must be full-time and attendance-based, and the applicant must not have resided in Germany for more than 15 months at the application deadline.
benefits: Monthly rent subsidy in certain circumstances
Monthly allowance for accompanying family members
Subsidy for justified additional costs in the case of disability or chronic illness
Green Mobility Top Up or reimbursement of carbon offset payments for air travel
German language course of 2, 4 or 6 months before the study programme if necessary
Allowance for a personally chosen German language course during the scholarship period
Reimbursement of the fee for a TestDaF or DSH test
coverage: Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Optional monthly allowance for accompanying family members
requirements: Applications are possible only between 1 June and the stated application deadline
All application documents must be submitted in German or English; other languages must be translated
Do not upload work samples to the DAAD portal - they go to the DAAD media database
The DAAD portal closes at 24.00 hrs (CET/CEST) on the last application day
Late or incomplete applications cannot be considered
documents: Full curriculum vitae in tabular form
Form 'Information about your preferred master programmes'
Letter of acceptance from the host university in Germany (if available)
Confirmation of supervision from a German university teacher (complementary studies without degree only)
Current transcript of records with individual grades
All university degree certificates indicating final grades
Proof of proficiency in the language of instruction
Samples of work uploaded to the DAAD media database
existing.english_requirement: Knowledge of the language of instruction of the chosen study programme at the latest by the start of the scholarship; language certificates may not be older than three years.
application_method: Complete the online application and upload the application documents
After the formal check, upload the work samples and supplementary list to the DAAD media database
existing.selection_notes: A special DAAD committee of university teachers from German art, music and film schools makes the final decision, based on the written application and the artistic work samples. There can be up to seven months between submission and notification.
existing.best_fit: Graduates in drama, theatre directing/dramaturgy, musical theatre, performance studies, dance or choreography who need a German arts university for a Master's course or a one-year advanced project.
existing.notes: This programme only funds projects in the artistic field of the Performing Arts. Applicants from Theatre and Dance Studies as academic disciplines, or artists with a scientific project, should use other DAAD scholarship programmes.
existing.duration: 10 to 24 months for a Master's/postgraduate degree course; one academic year (usually 12 months) for complementary studies without degree
existing.application_period: Applications for this scholarship programme are possible between 1 June and 15 October 2026
existing.deadline_display: 15 October 2026; selection in April 2027; funding begins from October 2027. The DAAD portal closes at 24.00 hrs (CET/CEST) on the last application day.

existing.description: Scholarship of the Heinrich Böll Foundation for international students who have completed their first degree abroad and intend to start a Master's degree in Germany, and for international PhD candidates who completed their graduate degree abroad. Applications are accepted in two rounds a year. Master's students funded by the Federal Foreign Office receive a base scholarship of EUR 992 per month plus a health insurance allowance of up to EUR 100 and optional components; PhD candidates funded by the Federal Foreign Office receive EUR 1,500 per month plus health insurance of up to EUR 200 per month. The funds come from the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR) and the Federal Foreign Office (AA).
eligibility: First degree completed abroad (Bildungsauslaender) before starting a Master's programme in Germany
Graduate degree completed abroad before starting a PhD in Germany
Priority for applicants from DAC countries who have not yet taken up residence in Germany at the time of application
AA-funded track requires a nationality from outside the EU; BMFTR track is aimed at German nationals, Bildungsauslaender educated in Germany and EU nationals
existing.eligibility_summary: International students who have completed their first degree abroad can apply before starting a Master's programme in Germany. International PhD students who completed their graduate degree abroad can apply for a PhD in Germany. Priority is given to applicants from DAC countries who have not yet taken up residence in Germany at the time of their application.
benefits: Reimbursement of German tuition fees up to EUR 10,000 per year (AA track)
Fixed fringe benefits of EUR 38 per month
Ideational support, events and alumni network offered by the foundation
coverage: Base scholarship of EUR 992 per month for master's students (AA track)
Base scholarship of EUR 1,500 per month for PhD candidates (AA track)
Health insurance allowance of up to EUR 100 per month (master's) or up to EUR 200 per month (PhD)
Reimbursement of tuition fees in Germany of up to EUR 10,000 per year
Tuition fees for German language courses
Fixed fringe benefits of EUR 38 per month
Family allowance and child allowances per child
BMFTR study grant of up to EUR 855 plus EUR 300 study costs
BMFTR PhD funding of EUR 1,650 plus EUR 100 and EUR 155 research costs and mobility allowance
requirements: Applications are accepted only online; the portal opens about six weeks before the deadline
The application deadline is 1 March and 1 September; the portal opens around 15 January and 15 July respectively
Parts of the degree programme may be completed abroad if academically necessary, but with no additional funding for studies abroad
Any additional income must be offset against the scholarship payment
documents: Completed online application in the Heinrich Böll Foundation scholarship portal
Application checklist for graduate students (PDF issued by the foundation)
Application checklist for PhD candidates (PDF issued by the foundation)
existing.english_requirement: The foundation runs its selection in German and English and publishes all application materials in both languages; no separate English certificate is listed on the scholarship pages.
application_method: Register in the Heinrich Böll Foundation online application portal when it opens
Complete the online application in full and upload the documents listed in the relevant application checklist
Submit before the closing date of the chosen round
existing.selection_notes: From the time of application (1 March or 1 September) the three-stage application process takes four to five months. Funding usually starts at the beginning of the winter term (applying by 1 March) or at the beginning of the summer semester (applying by 1 September), or somewhat earlier for PhD students.
existing.best_fit: Students and doctoral candidates from DAC and other non-EU countries who completed their first or graduate degree outside Germany and want to study or do a PhD in Germany.
existing.notes: The scholarship is funded by the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR) and the Federal Foreign Office (AA); the funding track determines the amount and the components. Any additional income must be offset against the scholarship payment, using the marginal-employment earnings limit under Section 8 (1) No. 1 SGB IV.
existing.application_period: 15 January 2027 to 1 March 2027, and 15 July 2027 to 1 September 2027
existing.deadline_display: Two rounds per year. Spring 2027: 15 January 2027 until 1 March 2027 (online portal opens 15 January 2027 and closes 1 March 2027). Fall 2027: 15 July 2027 until 1 September 2027.
